prompt:
Two young women stand side by side in a bright bedroom in front of a fitted cream wardrobe, facing camera, feet planted, both in sunglasses. Locked-off static camera, no pan, no zoom, no cuts.

The woman on the LEFT (dark hair in a low bun, butter-yellow oversized shirt, sage-green satin midi skirt) speaks to camera. The woman on the RIGHT (blonde wavy hair, sage-green ribbed tee, butter-yellow wide-leg trousers) does not speak — mouth closed, she blinks and shifts her weight slightly. Both pose naturally for camera and make small hand movements showing off their clothes.

SHE SAYS, ONCE, AND NOTHING ELSE: "Tizkeri, yellow and green olive ze sunny"

Israeli Hebrew with English colour words mixed in, the way Israelis actually talk — code-switching, completely natural, not translated.
Four stressed beats: tizke-RI / YEL-low / GREEN OL-ive / SUN-ny. Everything between them is light and unstressed.
Beat one: "tizkeRI," Hebrew, rising, landing on the last syllable, then a short breath at the comma.
Beats two and three: "yellow and green olive" — English words, clean English pronunciation, stress on YEL and on GREEN OL; the "and" is swallowed almost to nothing.
Beat four: "ze SUNny" — the Hebrew "ze" is light and the stress lands on SUN, then falls away.
The English words sit inside Hebrew rhythm — she is not switching languages, she is speaking Hebrew that happens to contain "yellow", "green olive" and "sunny".
Pace it conversational, about three seconds, warm and slightly amused — a friend telling you something obvious, not a presenter announcing it.

Photorealistic, real skin texture. No music, no on-screen text, no captions, no subtitles, no watermark.
